title: fix(mobile): Android terminal sends hardware-keyboard arrows, Tab, and Escape to the PTY
author: only21mil
head: e403b8c1169b7da6021ad8ac78d6d2be4004b77b
body:
## Problem

On Android, a hardware keyboard's arrow keys, Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape send nothing to the terminal. Shell history, Tab completion and arrow-driven TUIs (vim, htop, less, agent CLI prompts) cannot be used from the keyboard. These key events also go unconsumed, so Android can move focus off the terminal's hidden input. On an emulator, after Tab and Escape the next keys were lost until the terminal was tapped again.

The hidden `EditText`'s key listener only handles Backspace and Ctrl+A..Z. iOS already sends `ESC[A`..`ESC[D`, `\t`, `ESC[Z` and `ESC` for these keys (`TerminalHardwareKeyEncoder`).

## Change

- New `TerminalNavigationKeyListener` (same package and pattern as `TerminalEnterListener`) maps key-down to the iOS bytes: arrows to `ESC[A`/`ESC[B`/`ESC[C`/`ESC[D`, Tab to `\t`, Shift+Tab to `ESC[Z`, Escape to `ESC`. It also consumes the matching key-up, so no focus navigation runs.
- `T3TerminalView`'s existing key listener calls it after the read-only check. Read-only mode still swallows every key.
- Like iOS, it handles these keys only with no modifiers, plus Shift+Tab. Ctrl, Alt and Meta combinations keep today's behavior. No other keys change, and `hardwareKeyRevision` stays as is (nothing reads it, and the earlier Android key fixes did not bump it).

## Scope and approval

title: fix(shared): inline code like `allocator.cc:217` becomes a file chip
author: felixlaga
head: f1c80e047737df81ac31e4d0c6e86ff2f70a7321
body:
## Problem

In a chat message, inline code naming a bare C++ source with a line number, such as `allocator.cc:217`, stays plain code. The file-chip check lists `cc` with the generic TLDs (`com`, `dev`, …), so it reads the text as a host and port. ## Scope and approval

This is a very small fix for an obvious misclassification. It only affects bare file names, since `src/main.cc:12` already worked. It reaches every client that renders file chips from inline code (web, desktop, mobile, thread find). title: docs(updates): say when Update all leaves a provider out
author: Djordje-Stojanovic
head: 5ef34c559fe00d0a83715695b2aeced7af752cb8
body:
The provider update guide says only providers with a manual update command are left out of **Update all**. The code leaves out more than that. This PR makes the guide match the code. It changes no behavior.

## The defect

`hasOneClickUpdateProviderCandidate` in `apps/web/src/components/ProviderUpdateLaunchNotification.logic.ts` (lines 139-168 on `main` and at `v0.1.7`) checks every instance of a driver. It returns `false` for the whole driver when an enabled, outdated instance has no one-click command, or when outdated instances report different update commands. ## Problem

`materializePiT3McpExtension` wrote the T3 MCP extension directly to the shared cache path with `fs.writeFileString`, which truncates the file before writing. The reader of that file is an external process — the pi CLI loads the extension from disk when a session launches — so a pi process starting while the write is in flight reads an empty or partial file and starts with a broken extension.

Reproduced with two real processes hammering the real `materializePiT3McpExtension`: over 43,000 reads during repeated materializations, the reader saw the file **missing 54,612 times and empty 4,510 times** (the truncate-then-write window). The extension is written to a sibling staging file and renamed into place. The rename is atomic (same volume), so a reader always sees the previous file or the complete new one — never the truncated state.

No linked issue; filed under the small focused fix for an obvious bug. Three lines in one function plus a regression test; no API, caller, or product-behavior changes beyond the torn read being gone.

body:
## Problem

#29838 changed the usage-limit auto-resume to an agent message. If the server restarts after that resume is dispatched but before the provider starts it, startup recovery cancels the run. ** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win**

**Escape a backslash before the inserted break tag.**

A cell containing `path\\next` renders with one backslash and a line break. The serializers emit the text content as-is, so copying produces `path\next`. Markdown then treats `` as literal text instead of a break. Escape the preceding backslash when writing the break tag on both platforms. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/enriched-markdown/29ddd424/packages/react-native-enriched-markdown/android/src/main/java/com/swmansion/enriched/markdown/utils/common/serialization/MarkdownASTSerializer.kt))

** Minor** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win**

**Stop the quadratic backtracking on long backslash runs.**

`tableCellLineBreak` has no anchor. At each start position inside a run of backslashes, `(\\*)` consumes the rest of the run, fails at the missing `\n`, and backtracks one character at a time. A run of N backslashes that is not followed by a newline can take on the order of N²/2 steps.

`serializeTableCell` runs for every cell while `TableContainerView` builds `TableCellData`, with no newline guard. The cost can therefore occur during table rendering, even when the table is never copied. The iOS `markdownFromTableCellNode` uses the same pattern at line 84. That path runs only when the cell contains a newline.

Prevent matches from starting inside a run. A lookbehind does this. The leftmost match does not change, because a match always starts at the beginning of its backslash run.

Test a table cell that contains a long backslash run on both platforms, and measure the rendering time.

_Source: Coding guidelines_

title: fix(acp): bound unread raw notification retention
author: StiensWout
head: 5d1fa0afa30651e8fced9e143bab094f9860ef42
body:
## Problem

The raw ACP notification stream retained up to 32 payloads even when nobody read it. Synthetic 8 MiB notifications could pin roughly 252 MiB per connection.

## Change

Bound the unread raw backlog by both 32 entries and 16,777,216 UTF-16 code units of JSON line text, using parser data without re-encoding. Keep the newest notification even if it alone exceeds the budget. Typed notification handlers still receive every notification, and a raw reader that keeps up still receives everything.

The raw stream now drains and completes when the connection ends. This does not immediately clear an unread backlog. Non-Latin-1 text can require roughly twice the nominal character budget in memory; this is not a strict 16 MiB heap ceiling. Batch messages are conservatively charged for their entire JSON line.

## Scope and approval

Fixes #18799. This is a focused retention fix to the existing shared protocol queue, without changes to provider capabilities, wire schemas, or client flows. No application in this repository consumes the raw stream. The existing newest-entry policy and typed notification delivery are preserved.

## Verification

Primary validation and both fresh independent reviews passed all 69 focused protocol, client, agent and stdio tests. New public-stream cases cover unread eviction, an oversized newest notification, a reader that keeps up, EOF completion, scope closure and late input after a writer failure.
